main_text.p: ptura statuit,sed pepcrit coiectura hominum. quorum mentes superstitio credula occupa-verat, post animis superstitio audaciam indi-dit,ut de rebus ignotis pronunciarent,pedem inferentes in ea quæ non viderant, ut ait Pau-lus Col.2 18.temereq inflati carnis suæ intel-ligentia. De aliis locis insuper nihil dicam, quia hoc rei caput est, quod Bellarmino vsum est propugnare: nos vero non juvat litem ex lite nectere, qui veritatem in pace & sanctimonia colimus, vestigia Domini nostri persequetes. Quid enim nobis profuerit unguis, quod ai-unt, in ulcere? Cū itaq; hic de Purgatorio locus tanti apud illos videatur esse, ut multi non du-bitaverint immaneis quosdam centones ad probationem argumenti huius perscribere, & quiduis ad firmamentum causæ(si ullum esse potest) advocare; quorum exemplo & ductu Bel-larminus in idem scamma descedere coactus est, ut Rom. Ecclesiæ in hoc quoq; argumento subsidia sua contribuat: non potui quin ordi-ne illius servato sextam hanc controversi-am saltem aliquo modo destrigerem, & pau-cis quam modestissime per nos fieri potuit dogma istud lucrosum docentib. sed revera omnibus damnosum confutare. Cū autem duas huius tractationis partes Bellarminus nobis præformauerit: unam,ꝗ fit Purgatorii.

page.notes: Top line begins with a cut letter before "ptura"; the page opens mid-sentence, so the first word is kept as a fragment. The abbreviation before "fit" in the last line (printed like a q with a stroke) is doubtful: read as ꝗ, not certain. "temereq" is printed without a space; kept as printed. The text is set in roman with no printed indent at line starts, so it was taken as one paragraph. No page number or running head is printed. A stray mark at the very bottom edge is a scan artefact and was left out.
